summary.headline: Rishabh Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 4.2% to INR1,983 mn, with EBITDA up 17.3% to INR333 mn at a 16.8% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR1,983 mn (+4.2% YoY) and EBITDA INR333 mn (+17.3% YoY, 16.8% margin), after a INR20 mn ESOP/SAR charge; reported PAT was INR194 mn (-1.4% YoY) due to a INR20 mn rise in depreciation. The EEI segment was the engine: management cited 34% revenue growth and roughly 24% EBITDA margin, ahead of its ~20% top-line and 20-22% EBITDA guidance. Lumel Alucast remained a planned revenue decline (-41.2%) and was at operating breakeven with adjusted EBITDA of -6.4%. The company stayed net debt-free with net cash of INR1,606 mn.

segments.name: EEI (Electrical & Electronics Instrumentation)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 34% YoY with EBITDA margin around 24%, above the 20-22% guidance; management calls it the group's primary growth and profitability engine.

segments.name: Rishabh India (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR776 mn (+25.6%), EBITDA margin 22.9%; growth attributed to current transformers, data centres, solar and exports. Solar is under 5% of total and was about INR8-9 crore last year.

segments.name: Lumel S.A. (Poland)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR639 mn (+39%), adjusted EBITDA INR153 mn (24%), contributing about 50% of consolidated bottom line; one German grid-upgrade customer is roughly 20-25% of its sales.

segments.name: Lumel Alucast (HPDC)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR443 mn (-41.2%) as a planned decline; adjusted EBITDA -INR28 mn (-6.4%), at operating breakeven. Management targets adjusted EBITDA breakeven by end FY27 and double-digit margin over the medium term.

segments.name: US / UK / China and other international
segments.commentary: US and UK grew over 40% YoY and China 20.3%; US is about INR30 crore last year with INR45 crore targeted this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years on an organic basis. Management says these remain on a small base.

segments.name: Solar inverters
segments.commentary: Single-phase iUNO (up to 5 kW) reached operational profitability; 3-phase iNEO launched up to 12 kW this quarter, with up to 50 kW due by end FY27 and hybrid inverters in development. FY27 solar target is INR24-25 crore, rising to INR250-300 crore next year per management.

guidance_outlook: EEI guidance held at about 20% top-line growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin for the full year; management said it will try to beat this but did not raise it.
Lumel Alucast expected to reach adjusted EBITDA breakeven for full-year FY27; management sees a path to double-digit EBITDA margin in about 2 years.
US organic revenue target INR45 crore this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years.
Nashik plant to be fully finished in about 1-2 months; management targets more than 2.5x production over the next 4-5 years.
Mumbai and Delhi TMI Experience Centres to be operational by end of FY27; ~15 new products launched over two years with more than 15 planned for FY27.
CT capacity to rise from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 low-voltage units per day, with medium-voltage CTs to follow.
capex_capacity: New Nashik manufacturing facility partially commissioned; both buildings complete, with full completion expected in about 1-2 months.
Current transformer capacity being raised from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 low-voltage units per day (near-doubling), with added machinery already ordered.
Three SMT lines in PCB/EMS operations; latest is high-end and an older line is being upgraded. A fourth line will be added once the three run on three shifts.
Dedicated automated floor for solar inverter manufacturing in the new facility.
Lumel Alucast capacity is underutilised; management is filling it with higher-value orders.
demand_pricing: Domestic order bookings in Q1 were about 20% above last year, but billing lagged, leaving a backlog to be worked off.
Data-centre wins: first win announced, then 3-4 more; about 10 more quotes outstanding.

Lumel S.A. growth comes from product spread, German grid upgrades (EUR5 mn order executed; EUR3 mn follow-on running to year-end) and radiation-detection gates, with Poland security demand after the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Lumel Alucast: RFQs in advanced stages of commercial negotiation and customer approval; ramp-up takes about 6 months after award. Management is prioritising value over volume.
Solar inverter pricing is competitive with Chinese imports; EPC contractors are moving away from Chinese-sourced units over after-sales and warranty concerns.
Contribution margin is about 45% on average; solar and EMS run at 15-20%, while other products run at 40-75%.

financial_highlights.value: INR382 mn (24.8% margin, EEI basis as described)

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash and cash equivalents (30 June 2026)

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the 34% EEI growth, versus the 20-25% guidance, and is there lumpiness that will moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is spread across Rishabh India (current transformers, data centres, solar), Lumel S.A. (product spread, German grid upgrades) and new products, not one lumpy item. It reiterated EEI guidance of around 20% top-line and 20-22% EBITDA margin, saying it will try to beat it.

qa_highlights.question: How fast can the US business scale, and are there inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: US revenue went from about INR20 crore to INR30 crore last year, with INR45 crore targeted this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years organically. Actions include more sales staff, Mexico/Canada focus, UL/ANSI product redesigns, and a couple of inorganic opportunities under review.

qa_highlights.question: Lumel Alucast: what is the pipeline for returning to INR180-230 crore revenue and double-digit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: RFQs are in advanced commercial negotiation and customer approval; ramp-up takes about 6 months after award. Management sees double-digit EBITDA margin in about 2 years and says costs have been cut substantially.

qa_highlights.question: Will the quarterly EEI growth trajectory continue, and what about AI/data-centre traction in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is almost comparable to last year's Q4 and the company wants to beat guidance rather than raise it, citing seasonality in Europe and Diwali. Data-centre wins are one announced plus 3-4 more, with about 10 quotes outstanding; domestic bookings were about 20% higher YoY but billing lagged.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Lumel S.A. and India growth came from the German customer and from solar inverters?
qa_highlights.answer: The first EUR5 mn German order is already executed; the EUR3 mn follow-on runs to year-end, estimated at 20-25% of Lumel S.A. sales. Solar is under 5% of total, about INR8-9 crore last year, targeted at INR24-25 crore this year and INR250-300 crore next year; EEI contribution margin for solar and EMS is 15-20% versus about 45% average.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity and adjacencies: CT capacity, PCB/EMS, battery systems and M&A size?
qa_highlights.answer: CT capacity is moving from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 low-voltage units per day, with medium-voltage to follow. Three SMT lines run PCB/EMS, with a fourth once they hit three shifts. Battery systems will be indirect via hybrid inverters. Acquisitions considered in the INR50-200 crore range; about 4-5 targets under review, none at a serious stage.

risks_watch: EEI growth sustainability: management held guidance at about 20% top line and 20-22% EBITDA margin despite 34% Q1 growth; watch whether Q2-Q4 deliver and whether seasonality (European summer and winter holidays, Diwali) bites.
Lumel Alucast: still EBITDA-negative (-6.4% adjusted) with revenue down 41.2%; breakeven targeted by end FY27 and double-digit margin in about 2 years depends on RFQ conversion and a 6-month ramp.
Domestic billing lag: bookings about 20% above last year but billing has not caught up, leaving a backlog to work off.
Customer concentration: one German grid-upgrade customer is estimated at 20-25% of Lumel S.A. sales, with the EUR3 mn follow-on running only to year-end.

Solar scale-up risk: FY27 target of INR24-25 crore and next-year INR250-300 crore depends on iNEO 3-phase up to 12 kW and 50 kW models due by end FY27, plus hybrid inverters still in development; pricing is competitive with Chinese imports.
Margin and PAT pressure: consolidated PAT fell 1.4% YoY on a INR20 mn rise in depreciation, and ESOP/SAR costs of INR20 mn per quarter continue for about three more years.
key_quotes: So we see the growth coming out of multiple factors actually.
And this quarter, we have delivered more than that on the EEI business. And it will be around that or more throughout the year.
We want to keep our guidelines, which are already kind of aggressive, and we want to beat them by performance rather than giving guidelines which are a bit risky.
So any addition to the top line will very quickly reflect into the bottom line.
We're almost doubling our capacity, close to doubling our capacity.
summary.management_tone: Confident on EEI and Lumel S.A., with management repeatedly describing growth as broad-based and sustainable. Noticeably cautious on guidance, declining to raise the 20% top-line target and saying it prefers to beat guidance rather than give aggressive numbers. Lumel Alucast and US timelines were framed as a process needing time, and several answers on inorganic plans and forward numbers were deliberately non-committal.

Solar inverter 3-phase iNEO up to 50 kW due by end FY27 (dedicated automated floor in new facility)

growth.why: Management held EEI guidance at about 20% top-line growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin for FY27, with Q1 consolidated revenue up 4.2% (Lumel Alucast's planned -41.2% decline offsets EEI's 34% growth), domestic bookings about 20% higher, and a near-doubling of CT capacity plus new Nashik facility coming online.
